headline: Rain-hit Asian Games: Bangladesh reach semi-finals without playing a ball
summary: Bangladesh and Sri Lanka advance to the last four after quarter-finals are washed out due to heavy rain in Nagoya.
details: Bangladesh have reached the semi-finals of the men's Asian Games cricket tournament without bowling a single ball, as their quarter-final match against Malaysia was washed out.
The victory was awarded to Bangladesh because they were the higher-ranked team in the matchup, according to tournament rules for weather-related cancellations.
Sri Lanka similarly advanced to the semi-finals after their quarter-final clash with Nepal was also cancelled due to persistent wet weather in Nagoya and Aichi prefecture.
Bangladesh is now set to face Pakistan in the semi-finals, while Sri Lanka will take on India.
Both semi-final matches are scheduled for Thursday.
Heavy rain has disrupted several matches in the recent days, including Monday's games which were also washed out, though better weather is forecast from Wednesday.
caption:

Sri Lanka similarly advanced to the semi-finals after their quarter-final clash with Nepal was also cancelled due to persistent wet weather in Nagoya and Aichi prefecture.

Bangladesh is now set to face Pakistan in the semi-finals, while Sri Lanka will take on India.

Both semi-final matches are scheduled for Thursday.

headline_marked: Police arrest 18 in [[attacks on studio and health center]] in Dhaka
headline: Police arrest 18 in attacks on studio and health center in Dhaka
summary: The incidents involved looting at New Guinea Properties in ECB circle and the destruction of a health center in Mirpur.
details: Police have arrested 18 people in connection with attacks and looting at New Guinea Properties in the ECB circle of the capital and the destruction of a health center in Mirpur.
The attack on New Guinea Properties was reportedly triggered by a land dispute. Retired army officer Golam Mohiuddin Chowdhury is named as the mastermind behind the attack.
In the Mirpur incident, influential figures, including local BNP leader Hanif Mia and Abul Kalam Azad, are alleged to be involved.
Despite the arrests, police have stated that the masterminds or the primary architects behind both attacks have not yet been brought to justice.
caption:
18 arrested after violent attacks on a studio and a health center in Dhaka. The masterminds are still on the run.

Police have arrested 18 people in connection with attacks and looting at New Guinea Properties in the ECB circle of the capital and the destruction of a health center in Mirpur.

The attack on New Guinea Properties was reportedly triggered by a land dispute. Retired army officer Golam Mohiuddin Chowdhury is named as the mastermind behind the attack.

In the Mirpur incident, influential figures, including local BNP leader Hanif Mia and Abul Kalam Azad, are alleged to be involved.

Despite the arrests, police have stated that the masterminds or the primary architects behind both attacks have not yet been brought to justice.
